description: Expected PlanValidator outcome for every fixture in plans/. Person 4's integration tests and Person 1's policy tests can assert against this file instead of hardcoding codes. Enforced by services/atlas-core/tests/intent/test_published_fixtures.py, so a fixture cannot silently stop reproducing its rejection.

plans.note: The demo-path plan. Byte-compatible with packages/contracts/examples/plan.valid.json in shape; this is what the fixture planner emits for 'open my editor'.
Arbitrary shell execution. Blocked by category, so the user-facing reason is 'ATLAS cannot run shell commands' rather than 'unknown action'.
The model declared T0 for an action the registry fixes at T1. Master PRD 7: tiers are assigned by local code.
Plausible but unregistered action. Master PRD FR-03: unknown action types must be rejected.
Correct tier, but consent waived. The model cannot waive user approval.
timeoutMs above the registry ceiling for app.open (10000).
Without window.exists the result cannot be verified, so success could never be evidenced.
additionalProperties:false stops an invented field such as 'executeWithoutApproval' from reaching the runtime.
An extra 'commandLine' argument is how an app.open step would try to become shell execution. argumentsSchema forbids it.
Duplicate keys make retry-safety undecidable: a timeout could not be distinguished from a second intended action.

providerFixtures.note: OpenAI-compatible success body whose message content is a valid plan for taskId task-f001.
Plan wrapped in prose and a markdown fence. The planner must still extract it.
Model asks a question instead of planning (Master PRD FR-04).
HTTP 200 with no choices[0].message.content. Must produce MALFORMED_RESPONSE, never an empty success.
HTTP 200 carrying an application error. Must produce a provider failure, not a success.
A well-formed reply that reaches for a blocked action. Proves the gate, not the prompt, is the defence.
